chapter: Trios, electric questions and the big band
title: Running a big band
summary: Tyner talks of soloist personalities in a big band and how Ellington and Gillespie kept theirs going.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I’ve got in my hand now, this is your interest in big bands and maintaining a big band. Now I have an orchestra too and so does Ken and we know what the trials and tribulations are of running a big band. You really have to want to have a big band to do that.
Well my latest project was Coltrane. That was seventeen (laughs) so yeah that was a little rough.
He talks about that a lot.

Yeah you have to deal with a lot of personalities in a big band. You know a lot of guys want to solo they jump up. I used to like to point to a guy if I wanted to hear his instrument, but then another guy beats him and he stands up before him and I’m thinking, “I wanted to hear the other guy”. He sees me pointing to the other guy but he jumps up first. He says, “No I’m next buddy” (laughs). A lot of personalities there (laughs).
So you want to know how Duke and them did it all those years?
You’ve got to really love it.
Yeah well you’re traveling all the time together.

So this has to be a labor of love, you have to want to do this. So you must have said, “Well I want to have a big band” and you did it, is that how that came up? This is on Verve and this one is from ’92.
